layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The recent Segment Anything Model (SAM) represents a big leap in scaling up

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation models, allowing for powerful zero-shot capabilities and flexible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompting. Despite being trained with 1.1 billion masks, SAM's mask prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality falls short in many cases, particularly when dealing with objects that have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intricate structures. We propose HQ-SAM, equipping SAM with the ability to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurately segment any object, while maintaining SAM's original promptable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design, efficiency, and zero-shot generalizability. Our careful design reuses and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserves the pre-trained model weights of SAM, while only introducing minimal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additional parameters and computation. We design a learnable High-Quality Output

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Token, which is injected into SAM's mask decoder and is responsible for predicting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the high-quality mask. Instead of only applying it on mask-decoder features, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first fuse them with early and final ViT features for improved mask details. To train

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our introduced learnable parameters, we compose a dataset of 44K fine-grained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks from several sources. HQ-SAM is only trained on the introduced detaset of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 44k masks, which takes only 4 hours on 8 GPUs. We show the efficacy of HQ-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a suite of 10 diverse segmentation datasets across different downstream tasks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where 8 out of them are evaluated in a zero-shot transfer protocol. Our code and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pretrained models are at https://github.com/SysCV/SAM-HQ.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accurate segmentation of diverse objects is fundamental for a wide range of scene understanding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications, including image/video editing, robotic perception, and AR/VR. Trained with billion-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scale mask labels, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) [21] was recently released as a foundational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vision model for general image segmentation. SAM is capable of segmenting a wide range of objects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parts, and visual structures in diverse scenarios, by taking a prompt consisting of points, a bounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box, or a coarse mask as input. Its zero-shot segmentation abilities have led to a rapid paradigm shift,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as it can be transferred to numerous applications through simple prompting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While SAM has achieved impressive performance, its segmentation results are still unsatisfactory

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in many cases. In particular, SAM suffers from two key problems: 1) Coarse mask boundaries,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often even neglecting the segmentation of thin object structures, as shown in Figure 1. 2) Incorrect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predictions, broken masks, or large errors in challenging cases. This is often related to SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: misinterpreting thin structures, such as the kite lines in the rightmost column of Figure 1. These types

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of failures severely limit the applicability and effectiveness of foundational segmentation models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as SAM, in particular for automated annotation and image/video editing tasks, where highly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate image masks are crucial.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose HQ-SAM, which can predict highly accurate segmentation masks, even in very challeng-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing cases (see Figure 1), without compromising the strong zero-shot capabilities and flexibility of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Equal contribution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1: The predicted masks of SAM vs. our HQ-SAM, given the same red box or several points

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the object as input prompts. HQ-SAM produces significantly more detailed results with very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate boundaries. In the rightmost column, SAM misinterprets the thin structure of the kite lines,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and produces a large portion of errors with broken holes for the input box prompt.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: original SAM. To preserve the efficiency and zero-shot performance, we propose a minimal adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SAM, adding less than 0.5% parameters, to extend its capability to high-quality segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Directly fine-tuning the SAM decoder or introducing a new decoder module severely degrades the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general zero-shot segmentation performance. We therefore propose the HQ-SAM architecture, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tightly integrates with and re-uses the existing learned SAM structure, in order to fully preserve the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zero-shot performance. First, we design a learnable HQ-Output Token that is input to SAM's mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder, alongside the original prompt and output tokens. Unlike the original output tokens, our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-Output Token and its associated MLP layers are trained to predict a high-quality segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask. Second, instead of only re-using the SAM's mask decoder features, our HQ-Output Token

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: operates on a refined feature set to achieve accurate mask details. In particular, we use both global

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic context and local fine-grained features by fusing SAM's mask decoder features with early

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and late feature maps from its ViT encoder. During training, we freeze the entire pre-trained SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, while only updating our HQ-Output Token, its associated three-layer MLPs, and a small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature fusion block.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Learning accurate segmentation requires a dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with accurate mask annotations of diverse objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with complex and detailed geometries. SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is trained on the SA-1B dataset, which contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 11M images with 1.1 billion masks automatically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generated by a SAM-like model. However, us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing this extensive dataset presents significant cost

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: implications and falls short of achieving the de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sired high-quality mask generations pursued in our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work, as evident by SAM's performance in Fig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ure 1. Consequently, we compose a new dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: called HQSeg-44K, which contains 44K extremely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained image mask annotations. HQSeg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 44K is constructed by merging six existing image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets [35, 29, 26, 38, 8, 46] with highly accurate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask labels, covering over 1,000 diverse semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: classes. Thanks to the smaller-scale dataset and our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: minimal integrated architecture, HQ-SAM can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained in only 4 hours on 8 RTX 3090 GPUs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2: Performance vs. speed vs. model size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for an array of SAM variants [21, 52].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To validate the effectiveness of HQ-SAM, we perform extensive quantitative and qualitative experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mental analysis. We provide a comprehensive performance-speed-model size comparison on SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variants [21, 52] in Figure 2. We compare HQ-SAM with SAM on a suite of 10 diverse segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets across different downstream tasks, where 8 out of them are under a zero-shot transfer protocol,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including COCO [31], UVO [42], SGinW [58], LVIS [14], HQ-YTVIS [20], BIG [6], COIFT [29]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and HR-SOD [51]. This rigorous evaluation demonstrates that the proposed HQ-SAM can produce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher-quality masks while maintaining the zero-shot capability compared with SAM.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: High-quality Segmentation Existing works for high-quality segmentation are mostly trained for a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific segmentation task, like image and video instance segmentation [22, 19, 20, 40, 44], semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation [30, 54, 39, 50] or panoptic segmentation [9], in a close-world paradigm. Some of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them focus on post-segmentation refinement using with graphical models such as CRF [23] or region

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: growing [10]. However, the CRF-based refinement is adhere to low-level color boundaries without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully utilizing high-level semantic context and cannot fix large segmentation errors. While some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refinement-based works adopt separate deep networks for cascade iterative refinement [6, 37], they are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prone to overfitting as shown by our experiment. Compared to these high-quality segmentation [19

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 22, 33] or segmentation refinement methods, we focus on accurately segmenting diverse objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on new data with flexible prompting, and build a high-quality zero-shot segmentation model that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalizes to various segmentation tasks and domains. Unlike the post segmentation refinement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: works [6, 37], to preserve the zero-shot segmentation capability of SAM, HQ-SAM predicts the new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-quality mask directly by reusing the image encoder and mask decoder of SAM, instead of taking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the coarse mask and images as the input and feeding it into a separate refinement network. The model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: architecture of HQ-SAM builds upon SAM with negligible overhead, where we propose efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: token learning for accurate mask predictions. This is completely different from previous high-quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation works, and we show its effectiveness across a wide range of zero-shot experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fine-tuning and Prompt Tuning for Foundation Models Foundation models [2, 1] first appear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the NLP community, where large language models such as GPT series [2] show strong zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization to unseen tasks and data. Then, some prompt-based learning works [16, 27, 17] are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed to help these pre-trained models generalize to the downstream tasks instead of fine-tuning the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: internal model parameters [15] for better transfer learning. For vision-based foundation models [21,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 43, 59], prompt engineering [56, 45, 49, 57] that freezes the pre-trained model is first explored in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vision-language models, such as CLIP [36]. These prompts with learnable parameters are designed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to help downstream tasks with better context optimization. Different from the existing prompt-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or finetuning works, we focus on the minimal adaptation of SAM toward high-quality segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We directly use the proposed HQ-Output Token output for accurate mask prediction, instead of only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leveraging some learnable parameters [56] to help context learning and better generalization.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose HQ-SAM to upgrade SAM for high-quality zero-shot segmentation. HQ-SAM is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lightweight and only introduces two important adaptations to the SAM model. In Sec 3.1, we first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: briefly review the architecture of SAM on which HQ-SAM is built. Then, in Sec 3.2, we introduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our HQ-SAM with High-Quality Token (HQ-Output Token) and Global-local Feature Fusion, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are the key components to achieve better segmentation quality for SAM while preserving its zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capability. Finally, in Sec 3.3, we describe the training and inference process of HQ-SAM, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both data and computationally efficient.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Preliminaries: SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM [21] is composed of three modules: (a) Image encoder: a heavy ViT-based backbone for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image feature extraction, resulting in image embedding in spatial size 64×64. (b) Prompt encoder:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoding the interactive positional information from the input points/boxes/masks to provide for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask decoder. (c) Mask decoder: a two-layer transformer-based decoder takes both the extracted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image embedding with the concatenated output and prompt tokens for final mask prediction. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: released SAM model is trained on the large-scale SA-1B dataset, which contains over 1 billion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: automatically generated masks (400× more masks than any existing segmentation datasets [14, 24])

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 11 million images. Thus, SAM shows valuable strong zero-shot generalization to new data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without the necessity for additional training. However, we also note that SAM training is very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expensive, where distributively training ViT-H-based SAM for 2 epochs on SA-1B requires 256

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GPUs with a large batch size of 256 images. For more SAM method details, we refer readers to [21].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Ours: HQ-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section, we describe the architecture of the HQ-SAM network. To preserve the zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transfer capability of SAM, while preventing model overfitting or catastrophic forgetting, instead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of directly finetuning SAM or adding a new heavy decoder network, we take a minimal adaptation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach as much as possible. To this end, HQ-SAM reuses the pre-trained model weights of SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as much as possible with only two new key components, namely, High-Quality Output Token and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Global-local Feature Fusion, as illustrated in Figure 3. HQ-SAM can thus be regarded as a high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality zero-shot segmentation model evolved from SAM with negligible extra model parameters and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computation cost.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.1 High-Quality Output Token

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose efficient token learning for improving the mask quality of SAM. As shown in Figure 3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in SAM's original mask decoder design, the output token (similar to object query in DETR [3]) is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adopted for mask prediction, which predicts dynamic MLP weights and then performs point-wise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: product with the mask features. To promote SAM's mask quality in HQ-SAM, instead of directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: taking SAM's coarse masks as input, we introduce the HQ-Output token and a new mask prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer for high-quality mask prediction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In Figure 3, by reusing and fixing SAM's mask decoder, a new learnable HQ-Output Token (size

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 1×256) is concatenated with SAM's output tokens (size of 4×256) and prompt tokens (size of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the input to the SAM's mask decoder. Similar to the original output token, in each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attention layer, HQ-Output Token first performs self-attention with other tokens and then conducts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both token-to-image and the reverse image-to-token attention for its feature updating. Note that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-Output Token uses the point-wise MLP shared by the other tokens in each decoder layer. After

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passing through two decoder layers, the updated HQ-Output Token has access to the global image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context, the critical geometric/type information of prompt tokens as well as hidden mask information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the other output tokens. Finally, we add a new three-layer MLP to generate dynamic convolutional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: kernels from the updated HQ-Output Token, which then performs spatially point-wise product with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the fused HQ-feature for high-quality mask generation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Instead of directly finetuning SAM or further adding a heavy post-refinement network, we only allow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the HQ-Output Token and its associated three-layer MLPs to be trained for correcting the mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors of SAM's output token. This is completely different from existing high-quality segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models [19, 6, 20, 22]. We identify two main advantages of our efficient token learning through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extensive experiments: 1) This strategy significantly improves SAM's mask quality while only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: introducing negligible parameters compared to original SAM, making HQ-SAM training extremely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time and data-efficient; 2) The learned token and MLP layers do not overfit to mask the annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bias of a specific dataset, thus keeping SAM's strong zero-shot segmentation capability on new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images without catastrophic knowledge forgetting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2.2 Global-local Fusion for High-quality Features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Very accurate segmentation also requires input image feature with both rich global semantic context

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and local boundary details. To further promote mask quality, we enrich both the high-level object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: context and low-level boundary/edge information in the mask decoder features of SAM. Instead

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of directly using SAM's mask decoder feature, we compose the new high-quality features (HQ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Features) by extracting and fusing features from different stages of the SAM model: 1) The early

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer local feature of SAM's ViT encoder with spatial shape 64×64, which captures more general

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image edge/boundary details [12]. Concretely, we extract the feature after the first global attention

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: block of the ViT encoder, and for ViT-Large based SAM, this is the 6th block output for the 24 blocks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in total; 2) The final layer global feature of SAM's ViT encoder with shape 64×64, which has more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global image context information; 3) The mask feature in SAM's mask decoder with size 256×256,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is also shared by the output tokens, contains strong mask shape information.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Figure 3, to obtain the input HQ-Features, we first upsample the early-layer and final-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer encoder features to the spatial size 256×256 by transposed convolution. Then, we sum up these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three types of features in an element-wise manner after simple convolutional processing. We show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that this global-local feature fusion is simple while effective, yielding detail-preserving segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results with a small memory footprint and computation burden. We also perform detailed ablation on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the effect of each feature source in the experimental section (Table 3).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3 Training and Inference of HQ-SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training Data Construction To train HQ-SAM in a data-efficient manner, instead of further training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on SA-1B [21], we compose a new training dataset HQSeg-44K which contains 44,320 extremely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate image mask annotations. We note that the released SA-1B dataset only contains automatically

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generated mask labels, missing very accurate manual annotation on objects with complex structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Due to the annotation difficulty, HQSeg-44K leverages a collection of six existing image datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including DIS [35] (train set), ThinObject-5K [29] (train set), FSS-1000 [26], ECSSD [38], MSRA-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 10K [8], DUT-OMRON [46] with extremely fine-grained mask labeling, where each of them contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7.4K mask labels on average. To make HQ-SAM robust and generalizable to new data, HQSeg-44K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contains diverse semantic classes of more than 1,000. We show the advantage of using HQSeg-44K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by comparing HQ-SAM training with 44K randomly sampled images and masks from SA-1B [21] in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our supplemental analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-SAM Training During training, we fix the model parameters of the pre-trained SAM model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while only making the proposed HQ-SAM learnable. The learnable parameters thus only include the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-Output Token, its associated three-layer MLP and three simple convolutions for HQ-Features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion. Since SAM is designed for flexible segmentation prompts, we train HQ-SAM by sampling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mixed types of prompts including bounding boxes, randomly sampled points, and coarse masks input.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We generate these degraded masks by adding random Gaussian noise in the boundary regions of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GT masks. For generalizability to different object scales, we use large-scale jittering [13]. We use a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate of 0.001 and train our HQ-SAM for 12 epochs, with a learning rate drop after 10 epochs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We train on 8 Nvidia GeForce RTX 3090 GPUs with a total batch size of 32, which takes 4 hours to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: train for 16.6K iterations. Please refer to our supplemental file for more details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-SAM Inference We follow the same inference pipeline of SAM but use the mask prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from HQ-Output token as high-quality mask prediction. During inference, we sum the predicted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: logits of the SAM mask (by Output Token) and our predicted mask (by HQ-Output Token) for mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correction on spatial resolution 256×256. Then we up-sample the corrected mask to the original

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution 1024× 1024 as our output.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM vs. HQ-SAM on Training and Inference In Table 1, we report detailed training and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better segmentation quality, its training is very quick and affordable, which only takes 4 hours with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 8 RTX3090 GPUs. HQ-SAM is also lightweight and efficient, introducing negligible increases in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model parameters, GPU memory usage, and inference time per image.

layout_dets.text: 4 Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Experimental Setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Datasets For training we use the compiled HQSeg-44K, described in Section 3.3. For a comprehen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive evaluation of the segmentation performance of HQ-SAM, we perform experiments on a wide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of datasets, including four extremely fine-grained segmentation datasets: DIS [35] (validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set), ThinObject-5K [29] (test set), COIFT [29] and HR-SOD [51]. Besides, we experiment on popu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lar and challenging benchmarks across various image/video-based segmentation tasks in zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: settings, such as COCO [31], SGinW [58], UVO [42], LVIS [14], HQ-YTVIS [20] and BIG [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Evaluation Metrics To accurately quantify improvements in mask quality, instead of only employing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the standard mask AP or mask mIoU, we also adopt boundary metrics mBIoU and boundary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also evaluate on stricter Apstrict by adjusting the default dilation ratio from 0.02 to 0.01 on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UVO [42] and LVIS [14]. For evaluation on the four fine-grained segmentation datasets [35, 29, 51]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we also report the averaged boundary and mask IoU among them. For video instance segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation on HQ-YTVIS [20], we use both Tube Boundary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Tube Mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2 Ablation Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct detailed ablation studies on the proposed HQ-SAM using ViT-Large as the backbone,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analyzing the impact of the proposed HQ-Output Token and HQ-Features on segmentation quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially in zero-shot cases. For ablation experiments, we use the four aforementioned extremely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accurate segmentation datasets, namely, DIS (val) [35], ThinObject-5K (test) [29], COIFT [29] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HR-SOD [51] as well as the COCO validation set.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect of the High-Quality Output Token . HQ-SAM employs HQ-Output Token for high-quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask prediction. Table 2 compares our HQ-Output Token to the baseline SAM and other existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt/token learning strategies, such as adding an additional three context tokens [56] as learnable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vectors into the SAM's mask decoder for better context learning. Compared to using context tokens,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the HQ-Output token consistently brings larger performance gains on four high-quality datasets, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 13.2 mBIoU on DIS and 2.7 mBIoU on COIFT datasets. We also perform other ablation experiment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variants, such as computing the scaled dot product [18] between the original SAM's output token

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and our HQ-Output token or restricting the mask loss to only inside the boundary regions, and find

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they slightly decrease the averaged performance on the four evaluation datasets. Compared to SAM,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-SAM significantly improves the mBIoU on DIS benchmark from 52.8 to 70.4 and also promotes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mBIoU on the HRSOD dataset for 3.8 points.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ablation on the Global-local Fusion for HQ-Features Table 3 tabulates the effect of global-local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion, where the importance of each feature component is analyzed in HQ-Features during the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion process. Compared to directly using the mask decoder feature of SAM, the entire HQ-Features

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bring an obvious advantage of 2.6 mBIoU on four highly accurate segmentation datasets. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: final-layer ViT encoder feature with global context increases the mBIoU from 80.1 to 81.3. while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the early-layer feature with local details further promotes the mBIoU to 81.8. We also replace the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed global-local fusion with the conventional FPN to build a feature pyramid for fusion, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found this brought an inferior performance, decreasing from 89.1 to 87.4 mIoU.

layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose HQ-SAM, the first high-quality zero-shot segmentation model by introducing negligible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: overhead to the original SAM. We propose a lightweight High-quality Output Token in HQ-SAM to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: replace the original SAM's output token for high-quality mask prediction. After training only on 44K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: highly-accurate masks, HQ-SAM significantly boosts the mask prediction quality of SAM, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was trained on 1.1 billion masks. The zero-shot transfer evaluation is performed on 8 segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benchmarks across both image and video tasks, spanning diverse objects and scenes. Our research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: offers timely insights into how to leverage and extend SAM-like foundational segmentation models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a data-efficient and computation-affordable manner.

layout_dets.text: Training Details During training HQ-SAM on the composed HQSeg-44K, we fix the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters of the pre-trained SAM model while only making the proposed HQ-SAM learnable,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fusion. Two of them are transposed convolutions (size 2×2, stride 2) used to upscale encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . We treat the new HQ-Output Token as the fifth mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: token compared to the original four mask tokens in SAM's mask decoder. During training, this new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (size of 1 ×256) and prompt tokens (size of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the input to the SAM's mask decoder.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input and output shape for the 2-layer mask decoder of SAM is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . For experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using ViT-B, ViT-L, and ViT-H-based models on training, we adopt the same training setting, with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a learning rate of 1e-3 and train our HQ-SAM for 12 epochs (learning rate drops to 1e-4 after 10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: epochs). We supervise mask prediction of the new HQ-Output token with a combination of both BCE

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Loss and Dice Loss.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Implementation Details We follow the same inference pipeline of SAM but use the mask prediction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from HQ-Output token as high-quality mask prediction. Table 10 reports the detailed inference speed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparison using various backbones. For box-prompting-based evaluation, we feed SAM and our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HQ-SAM with the same image/video bounding boxes and adopt the single mask output mode of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM. For interactive segmentation comparison using a single point, we follow SAM and adopt the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: “center" point of Ground Truth (GT) masks, which is at a maximal value location in a mask's interior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distance transform. For multiple-point evaluation, we randomly sample the points from the GT masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and report the averaged results with three trials.

layout_dets.text: 8 More Details of HQSeg-44K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data compostion of HQSeg-44K In Table 14, we provide more details of our composed new training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset HQSeg-44K which contains 44,320 extremely accurate image mask annotations, where we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: show their annotation quality in Figure 8. HQSeg-44K is a collection of six existing image datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including DIS [35] (train set), ThinObject-5K [29] (train set), FSS [26], ECSSD [38], MSRA-10K [8],

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DUT-OMRON [46] with extremely fine-grained mask labeling, where each of them contains 7.4K

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask labels on average. This composed training set has no images/annotations overlapping with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zero-shot evaluation datasets adopted in our paper.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Effect of HQSeg-44K In Table 15, we show the advantage of using HQSeg-44K by comparing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the four datasets from 71.1 to 70.1, while ours improves it from 71.1 to 81.8. This validates

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the effectiveness of our constructed HQSeg-44K benchmark in improving mask quality. Note that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the ablation experiments in Table 2, Table 3, Table 4, and Table 9 of the paper are all based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constructed HQSeg-44K.
